question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{-2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}{6{x}^{3}-9} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{-2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{6{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{9}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(-2+\frac{1}{x})}{(6-\frac{9}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{-2+0}{6-0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity: Rational Solutions
question.worked_solution:
For large positive values of $x,$ we have $|7x-4|=7x-4.$ Consequently, for $x\to \infty ,$ we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{|7x-4|}{2x-6}={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{7x-4}{2x-6}.
$$

First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{1}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{7x-4}{2x-6} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{7x}{x}-\frac{4}{x})}{(\frac{2x}{x}-\frac{6}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(7-\frac{4}{x})}{(2-\frac{6}{x})} \\  & =\frac{7-0}{2-0} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Horizontal Asymptote of a Rational Function
question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{2x+5}{2{x}^{3}+2x+6}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2x+5}{2{x}^{3}+2x+6} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2x}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{2x}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{6}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})}{(2+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{6}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{0+0}{2+0+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$

question.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has No Horizontal Asymptote
question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{8{x}^{4}+x-2}{6x-5}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{8{x}^{4}+x-2}{6x-5} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{8{x}^{4}}{x}+\frac{x}{x}-\frac{2}{x})}{(\frac{6x}{x}-\frac{5}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(8{x}^{3}+1-\frac{2}{x})}{(6-\frac{5}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(8{x}^{3}+1-0)}{(6-0)} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(8{x}^{3}+1) \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{12x-3{x}^{4}}{3{x}^{2}+7}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{12x-3{x}^{4}}{3{x}^{2}+7} \\  & {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{3{x}^{4}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12}{x}-3{x}^{2})}{(3+\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{0-3{x}^{2}}{3+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(-{x}^{2}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
